_comment: TEXTS REGISTRY. Every text on the timeline is registered here by ID with its scholarly date range, a credible source, and either an imported copy (data/texts/<id>.txt) or an external link. Timeline events in the per-tradition files reference these IDs. Dates are SIGNED years: negative = BCE, positive = CE, year_from < year_to. Never present disputed dates as settled — use the certainty field.

date_range.note: Sayings were recorded by disciples and compiled over the Warring States period; the received text's stratification is debated.

analects.title: Analects of Confucius
analects.what: The Lunyu: short sayings and dialogues of Confucius and his disciples on ritual, family, government, and character — the core text of the Confucian tradition, later one of the Four Books.

date_range.note: Carved on pillars and rocks across the Mauryan empire in the local scripts and languages — including Greek and Aramaic in the northwest.

ashoka-edicts.source_label: Access to Insight — The Edicts of King Asoka
ashoka-edicts.title: Edicts of Ashoka
ashoka-edicts.what: Royal inscriptions proclaiming dhamma — tolerance, nonviolence, welfare works, and respect for all sects — the earliest decipherable Indian inscriptions.

date_range.note: Redacted in Sasanian Babylonia; its layers of debate span roughly the 3rd–6th centuries CE. A Jerusalem Talmud also exists (c. 400 CE).

babylonian-talmud.title: Babylonian Talmud
babylonian-talmud.what: Centuries of rabbinic debate (Gemara) around the Mishnah, interleaved with story, folklore, and law — the central text of rabbinic Judaism.

content.label: Read the declaration at Yale's Avalon Project

date_range.note: A letter from Foreign Secretary Arthur Balfour to Lord Rothschild, dated 2 November 1917, later incorporated into the League of Nations Mandate for Palestine.

balfour-declaration.source_label: Avalon Project, Yale Law School — Balfour Declaration
balfour-declaration.title: Balfour Declaration
balfour-declaration.what: The British government's statement supporting 'the establishment in Palestine of a national home for the Jewish people' — a foundational document in the history of modern Israel.

content.label: Read the Bhagavad Gita (public domain translations)

date_range.note: A dialogue within Book 6 of the Mahabharata; scholars place its composition in the last centuries BCE or the first centuries CE.

bhagavad-gita.title: Bhagavad Gita
bhagavad-gita.what: On the eve of battle, Krishna teaches Arjuna about duty, disciplined action, devotion, and liberation — 700 verses that became Hinduism's most-read and most-commented scripture.

date_range.note: 1 Maccabees was composed in Hebrew (now lost) around 100 BCE, covering 175–134 BCE; 2 Maccabees is an epitome of a longer Greek work.

books-of-maccabees.title: Books of the Maccabees
books-of-maccabees.what: Historical books recounting the Maccabean revolt and the Hasmonean kingdom. Canonical in Catholic and Orthodox Bibles; treated as apocrypha in Jewish and Protestant traditions.

content.label: Read The City of God at CCEL

date_range.note: Written 413–426 in response to the sack of Rome (410); Augustine died in 430 as the Vandals besieged his city of Hippo.

city-of-god.source_label: Christian Classics Ethereal Library — Augustine, City of God
city-of-god.title: Augustine, The City of God
city-of-god.what: Augustine's vast argument that history is the tale of two cities — the earthly city of self-love and the City of God — foundational for Western theology and political thought.

content.label: Read the UCL overview and translations

date_range.note: First Intermediate Period through the Middle Kingdom; painted inside non-royal coffins.

coffin-texts.source_label: UCL Digital Egypt for Universities — Coffin Texts
coffin-texts.title: Coffin Texts
coffin-texts.what: Some 1,185 funerary spells adapting Pyramid Texts material for non-royal dead — the afterlife democratized — and introducing the judgment of the dead before Osiris.

date_range.note: Scrolls copied between the 3rd century BCE and 68 CE and hidden in the Qumran caves; they include the oldest surviving manuscripts of the Hebrew Bible.

dead-sea-scrolls.source_label: Israel Antiquities Authority — Leon Levy Dead Sea Scrolls Digital Library
dead-sea-scrolls.title: Dead Sea Scrolls
dead-sea-scrolls.what: Some 900 manuscripts from the Qumran caves: biblical books, sectarian rules, prayers, and apocalyptic writings of a Jewish community of the late Second Temple period.

content.label: Read the Gathas, tr. L. H. Mills (1898, public domain PDF)

date_range.note: No scholarly consensus. Linguistic parallels with the Rig Veda point to the mid-to-late 2nd millennium BCE (Boyce, Hintze); other scholars allow dates as late as the 6th century BCE.

gathas.title: Gathas of Zarathustra
gathas.what: 17 hymns in Old Avestan traditionally attributed to Zarathustra himself — the oldest layer of the Avesta. They preach one Wise Lord (Ahura Mazda), the choice between truth (asha) and the lie (druj), and individual judgment after death.

date_range.note: Al-Bukhari (810–870) is said to have sifted some 600,000 reports over decades of travel; the Sahih's final form dates to the end of his life.

hadith-bukhari.title: Sahih al-Bukhari (Hadith)
hadith-bukhari.what: The most authoritative Sunni collection of hadith — reports of Muhammad's words, deeds, and approvals, each with a chain of transmission (isnad).

content.label: Scholarly discussion (cuneiform text held by the Oxford ETCSL corpus)

date_range.note: Earliest tablets from Abu Salabikh (Early Dynastic IIIa); the text was copied in scribal schools for over a millennium, so later copies do not date the composition.

instructions-of-shuruppak.source_label: N. Samet, 'The Sumerian proverb collections' — on the Early Dynastic Instructions of Shuruppak (ResearchGate)
instructions-of-shuruppak.title: Instructions of Shuruppak
instructions-of-shuruppak.what: One of the oldest known works of wisdom literature: proverbial instructions from King Shuruppak to his son Ziusudra, the Sumerian flood hero.

date_range.note: Jain teaching was transmitted orally for centuries; the Shvetambara canon was written down at Valabhi (c. 453–466 CE). Digambaras hold that the original canon was lost.

jain-agamas.title: Jain Agamas
jain-agamas.what: The canonical scriptures of Shvetambara Jainism: sermons of Mahavira and the early teachers, monastic discipline, cosmology, and narrative — in Ardhamagadhi Prakrit.

date_range.note: Written in Rome in the 70s CE by the former Jewish commander turned Flavian client, Josephus; our main narrative source for the destruction of Jerusalem.

josephus-jewish-war.source_label: Internet Sacred Text Archive — Works of Flavius Josephus
josephus-jewish-war.title: Josephus, The Jewish War
josephus-jewish-war.what: Josephus's account of the Jewish revolt against Rome (66–73 CE) and the burning of the Second Temple — apologetic and self-serving in places, indispensable nonetheless.

date_range.note: Composed and expanded over roughly eight centuries; the critical edition (Poona) reconstructs the oldest recoverable text from thousands of manuscripts.

mahabharata.title: Mahabharata
mahabharata.what: One of the longest poems ever written — the Bharata princes' fratricidal war, interwoven with law, myth, statecraft, and philosophy; it contains the Bhagavad Gita.

date_range.note: Composed over many centuries across India and Central Asia; the earliest, the Perfection of Wisdom (Prajnaparamita) literature, dates to around the turn of the era.

mahayana-sutras.title: Mahayana Sutras
mahayana-sutras.what: A vast family of scriptures — Perfection of Wisdom, Lotus, Pure Land, and Vimalakirti sutras among them — revered across Mahayana Buddhism.

content.label: Read the Masnavi at Dar al-Masnavi

date_range.note: Dictated by Rumi from c. 1258 until his death in 1273 and left unfinished; six books of rhyming couplets in Persian.

masnavi.title: Rumi, Masnavi
masnavi.what: Some 26,000 couplets of story, parable, and ecstatic commentary on divine love — often called 'the Quran in Persian' by admirers.

date_range.note: Compiled by Mencius and his disciples in the late Warring States period; canonized by Zhu Xi among the Four Books in the 12th century CE.

mencius.source_label: Internet Sacred Text Archive — Confucianism (the Four Books)
mencius.title: Mencius
mencius.what: The teachings of Mencius (Mengzi), the 'second sage' of Confucianism: human nature is good, and rulers who fail the people's welfare forfeit the Mandate of Heaven.

date_range.note: Compiled c. 200 CE by Judah ha-Nasi in Galilee; individual teachings are attributed to rabbis of the preceding two centuries.

mishnah.title: Mishnah
mishnah.what: The first major written compilation of the oral Torah: 63 tractates of law and practice — agriculture, festivals, family law, damages, sacrifices, purity.

content.label: Read the Mishneh Torah at Sefaria

date_range.note: Completed c. 1180 in Egypt; Maimonides also wrote the Guide for the Perplexed (c. 1190) for readers torn between Torah and philosophy.

mishneh-torah.title: Maimonides, Mishneh Torah
mishneh-torah.what: A complete, systematically organized code of Jewish law in fourteen books — the most ambitious codification of the medieval period.

content.label: Read the New Testament (public domain translations)

date_range.note: Paul's letters (c. 50–62) precede the Gospels (c. 65–100); individual books' dates are debated within these ranges.

new-testament.source_label: Internet Sacred Text Archive — The Bible
new-testament.title: New Testament
new-testament.what: The Christian scriptures: four Gospels, the Acts of the Apostles, letters of Paul and others, and Revelation — written in Greek across the Roman world.

content.label: Read the council's documents and creed

date_range.note: Adopted at Nicaea in 325 and expanded at Constantinople in 381; the form used in worship today is the Constantinopolitan text.

nicene-creed.source_label: New Advent — Documents of the First Council of Nicaea
nicene-creed.title: Nicene Creed
nicene-creed.what: The defining statement of Trinitarian orthodoxy: one God, Father, Son 'of one substance with the Father', and Holy Spirit — still recited across Catholic, Orthodox, and many Protestant churches.

date_range.note: Dated 31 October 1517, when Luther sent the theses to Archbishop Albrecht of Mainz; the famous nailing to the Wittenberg church door is first reported decades later and may be legendary.

ninety-five-theses.title: Luther, Ninety-Five Theses
ninety-five-theses.what: Ninety-five propositions against the sale of indulgences, meant for academic debate; printed and translated, they became the spark of the Reformation.

date_range.note: Late Shang dynasty, Anyang (Yinxu); Wu Ding-era bones radiocarbon dated to 1254–1197 BCE.

oracle-bone-inscriptions.source_label: Indiana University ScholarWorks — Glossed Texts for the Study of Shang Oracle Bone Inscriptions
oracle-bone-inscriptions.title: Oracle-bone inscriptions
oracle-bone-inscriptions.what: Divination records carved on ox scapulae and turtle plastrons — the earliest Chinese writing. Shang kings queried ancestors and high gods about harvests, warfare, and ritual.

content.label: Read the Pali Canon at Access to Insight

date_range.note: Teachings were preserved orally for centuries and written down in Sri Lanka in the 1st century BCE; the canon was edited and closed over a long period.

pali-canon.title: Pali Canon (Tipitaka)
pali-canon.what: The scriptural canon of Theravada Buddhism: the Buddha's discourses (Sutta), monastic discipline (Vinaya), and systematic philosophy (Abhidhamma), in the Pali language.

date_range.note: The oldest (Brihadaranyaka, Chandogya) are prose compositions of the mid-1st millennium BCE; they close the Vedic corpus as 'Vedanta', the end of the Veda.

principal-upanishads.source_label: Internet Sacred Text Archive — The Upanishads (Sacred Books of the East)
principal-upanishads.title: Principal Upanishads
principal-upanishads.what: Dialogues and speculations on atman (self) and brahman (ultimate reality), karma, rebirth, and liberation — the seedbed of later Hindu philosophy.

date_range.note: Eighteen major Puranas took shape mainly in the Gupta and early medieval centuries, incorporating much older material; dating any single Purana is approximate.

puranas.title: Puranas
puranas.what: Vast Sanskrit compendia of myth, genealogy, cosmology, pilgrimage, and devotion centered on Vishnu, Shiva, and the Goddess — the storybook of temple Hinduism.

date_range.note: Inscribed in the pyramids of Unas (24th c. BCE) through the 6th Dynasty at Saqqara; internal evidence suggests some spells preserve older oral material.

pyramid-texts.source_label: Internet Sacred Text Archive — The Pyramid Texts, tr. Samuel A. B. Mercer (1952)
pyramid-texts.title: Pyramid Texts
pyramid-texts.what: Funerary spells inscribed on the walls of Old Kingdom royal pyramids — the oldest extensive religious literature from ancient Egypt, guiding the king's ascent to the afterlife.

date_range.note: By Muslim tradition the revelation spans 610–632; the consonantal text was standardized under Caliph Uthman (c. 650s). Academic dating of individual surahs varies.

quran.title: Quran
quran.what: Islam's scripture: 114 surahs recited to Muhammad, in Muslim belief the literal word of God — law, story, warning, and worship in rhythmic Arabic prose.

date_range.note: Scholarly consensus (Flood, Witzel, Anthony) places the bulk of the hymns c. 1500–1200 BCE; some scholars widen the range to 1700–1100 BCE. Composed orally, committed to writing much later.

rig-veda.source_label: Internet Sacred Text Archive — Rig Veda, tr. Ralph T. H. Griffith (1896)
rig-veda.title: Rig Veda
rig-veda.what: 1,028 hymns in Vedic Sanskrit by priestly families of the Sapta-Sindhu region, preserved by exacting oral transmission. Centers on rta (cosmic order), sacrifice, and gods such as Indra and Agni.

content.label: Read Benedictine and early Christian texts

date_range.note: Traditionally written at Monte Cassino in the decades before Benedict's death (c. 547); its precise compositional history is debated.

rule-of-benedict.title: Rule of St Benedict
rule-of-benedict.what: Seventy-three short chapters ordering monastic life — prayer, work, reading, obedience, humility — that became the default constitution of Western monasticism.

date_range.note: 305 poems dated from the 11th to 7th centuries BCE; the collection was traditionally said to have been edited by Confucius.

shijing.source_label: Internet Archive — The She King, tr. James Legge (1871), scanned from the Chinese Classics
shijing.title: Shijing (Classic of Poetry)
shijing.what: The oldest collection of Chinese poetry: folk songs, court odes, and temple hymns including sacrificial odes to royal ancestors. Became one of the Confucian Five Classics.

content.label: Read the Summa at New Advent

date_range.note: Left unfinished at Aquinas's death in 1274; he reportedly stopped writing after a mystical experience in December 1273.

summa-theologiae.title: Aquinas, Summa Theologiae
summa-theologiae.what: The summit of scholastic theology: thousands of articles in question-and-answer form, arguing Christian doctrine through Aristotelian philosophy.

content.label: Read the Tao Te Ching (Legge translation)

date_range.note: Attributed to Laozi, probably a legendary figure; bamboo-slip fragments from Guodian (c. 300 BCE) are the oldest witnesses, and the received text took shape across the Warring States period.

tao-te-ching.source_label: Internet Sacred Text Archive — Tao Te Ching, tr. James Legge
tao-te-ching.title: Tao Te Ching
tao-te-ching.what: Eighty-one brief chapters on the Dao — the way that can be named is not the eternal way — and on rule by wu wei, action without forcing. Foundational for Daoism and beloved far beyond it.

date_range.note: Umasvati (Umasvami) is variously dated between the 2nd and 5th centuries CE; the sutra is the first Jain work in Sanskrit.

tattvartha-sutra.title: Umasvati, Tattvartha Sutra
tattvartha-sutra.what: A terse, systematic summary of Jain doctrine — the seven tattvas (soul, non-soul, influx, bondage, stoppage, shedding, liberation) — accepted as authoritative by both Digambaras and Shvetambaras.

date_range.note: Attributed to Enheduanna, daughter of Sargon of Akkad (c. 2334–2279 BCE) and high priestess of Nanna at Ur; authorship is traditional rather than proven.

temple-hymns-enheduanna.source_label: Jacket2 (University of Pennsylvania) — commentary and translation by Betty De Shong Meador
temple-hymns-enheduanna.title: Temple Hymns of Enheduanna
temple-hymns-enheduanna.what: 42 hymns addressed to the temples of Sumer, attributed to Enheduanna — the earliest named author in world literature.

date_range.note: The Torah's sources span the early 1st millennium BCE; most scholars date its final, Persian-era editing to the 5th–4th centuries BCE. Traditional attribution to Moses is a matter of faith.

torah.title: Torah (Pentateuch)
torah.what: The five books of Moses — Genesis through Deuteronomy: creation, the patriarchs, the Exodus, and the Law. Core scripture of Judaism and first section of the Hebrew Bible (Tanakh).

content.label: Read the council documents at vatican.va

date_range.note: The council sat in four sessions, 1962–65, under Popes John XXIII and Paul VI, issuing 16 documents.

vatican-ii-documents.source_label: The Vatican — Second Vatican Council archive
vatican-ii-documents.title: Second Vatican Council documents
vatican-ii-documents.what: Constitutions, decrees, and declarations of Vatican II — including Sacrosanctum Concilium (liturgy), Lumen Gentium (the Church), Nostra Aetate (other religions), and Dignitatis Humanae (religious liberty).

date_range.note: Core Zhouyi layers built up during the Western Zhou; exact stratification is debated. The Ten Wings commentaries are later (Warring States/Han).

yijing.source_label: Internet Sacred Text Archive — The Yî King, tr. James Legge (1882)
yijing.title: Yijing (I Ching / Book of Changes)
yijing.what: A divination manual of 64 hexagrams with judgments and line statements, later expanded into a cosmology of change.
